title: What's new in E-Documents: Overview
summary: This video introduces EDI support in Business Central 2026 release wave 2, built on top of the existing E-Documents framework. It explains the buyer and seller flow: purchase order, automatic sales order, order response and remittance advice. Ken covers the setup requirements, then Milita demos the full flow manually with the PEPPOL format across two companies. The last part shows that the same e-document and message architecture is used for three new French regulatory formats, with lifecycle events stored as messages linked to the invoice e-document.

features.name: EDI in Business Central
features.description: EDI is added to exchange order information between buyer and seller instead of sending email. It is built on the existing E-Documents technology and the PEPPOL format, with a log for each exchange.
caveats: The demo exchanges files manually by exporting and importing XML.
prerequisites: Standard e-document setup in both companies

features.name: Purchase order e-document (outbound)
features.description: When the buyer releases a purchase order, an e-document is generated in the background to send to the seller. It carries items, quantities and expected dates.
prerequisites: Purchase order document type added to the e-document service in the buyer company
Vendor set up to exchange files electronically

features.name: Automatic sales order from inbound e-document
features.description: On the seller side, importing the purchase order XML in the inbound e-document list with the PEPPOL format automatically creates a sales order. Dates, items, quantities and amounts are carried over.
prerequisites: Customer set up to exchange files electronically

features.name: Order response (accept or reject)
features.description: The seller can accept or reject the order and send a response back. The buyer imports it and it is linked to the original purchase order e-document with a status.
caveats: The demo only shows the accepted response type.

features.name: Remittance advice from payment journal
features.description: After posting the purchase invoice and applying a payment in the payment journal, the buyer can send a remittance advice file to the seller through the e-document service.
prerequisites: Remittance advice document type added to the e-document service in the buyer company

features.name: New e-document types and directions
features.description: Four e-document types are covered: purchase order, sales order, order response and remittance advice. Each document type can be set to inbound only, outbound only or both.

features.name: EDI setup requirements
features.description: Setup follows the same pattern as invoicing: standard e-document setup, vendor and customer set to exchange electronically, and electronic identifiers on both sides. Item reference or GTIN is recommended for items, and quantities and delivery dates should be filled.
caveats: Item reference or GTIN is recommended so items match on both sides.
prerequisites: Vendor and customer set up for electronic exchange
Electronic identifiers (GLN or VAT registration number)

features.name: E-document linkage from documents
features.description: New linkage functionality lets users open the created e-document straight from the purchase order via the fact box. The response messages can also be seen directly from the document.

features.name: E-document messages (acknowledgement and response)
features.description: A message architecture attaches messages such as acknowledgement and order response to the e-document. These messages are linked to the original document.

features.name: French regulatory e-document formats and lifecycle messages
features.description: Three new e-document formats for France are added, set up on the e-document service as other formats, including e-reporting. Lifecycle events such as collected, submitted, accepted, refused and technical rejected are stored as messages linked to the invoice e-document.
caveats: Applying a customer payment creates a collected message and unapplying creates a negative collected message.
prerequisites: The three formats are set up on the e-document service as other formats
